h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר י״א Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Yud Aleph
"We Were Slaves" on Shabbos HaGadol: Shabbos Brings Out of Mitzrayim

p: אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
It is stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' כ"ט.):
אֲבָל אִינּוּן חַיָּיבַיָּא דְּלָא מִשְׁתַּדְּלָן בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וּמִצְוֹת וְכוּלֵּי,
"But those wicked ones who do not exert themselves in Torah and mitzvos, etc.,
אִינּוּן עַבְדִּין לְאוּמִּין דְּעָלְמָא וּמִשְׁתַּעְבְּדִין בְּהוֹ, כְּגוֹן: עֲבָדִים הָיִינוּ לְפַרְעֹה בְּמִצְרָיִם;
they are slaves to the nations of the world and are subjugated to them, as in 'We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt';
וְאִי נָטְרוּ שַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים, אִתְּמַר בְּהוֹ: וַיּוֹצִיאֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ,
but if they guard Shabbasos and Festivals, it is said of them: 'And Hashem our God brought us out,'
וְיִתְקַיֵּים בְּהוֹ: לְמַעַן יָנוּחַ שׁוֹרְךָ וְגוֹמֵר וּבְהֶמְתֶּךָ
and there is fulfilled in them: 'So that your ox and your donkey may rest, etc., and your beast'
עַם הָאָרֶץ אִיקְרוּ בְּהֵמָה וְכוּלֵּי.
for the unlearned are called 'beast,' etc."
פֶּסַח הוּא זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
Pesach is a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt,
וְכָאן אָמַר דִּבְכָל יוֹם טוֹב וְשַׁבָּת אִתְּמַר בְּהוֹ: וַיּוֹצִיאֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ!
yet here it says that regarding every Festival and Shabbos it is said of them, "And Hashem our God brought us out"!
וּבֶאֱמֶת בְּכָל יוֹם טוֹב וְאַף בְּשַׁבָּת אוֹמְרִים "זֵכֶר לִיצִיאַת מִצְרָיִם",
And in truth, on every Festival and even on Shabbos we say "a remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt,"
וְהָיָה רָאוּי לוֹמַר רַק בְּפֶסַח
whereas it would seem fitting to say it only on Pesach
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שָׁבוּעוֹת זֵכֶר לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, וְכֵן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה זִכָּרוֹן לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן, וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְחִילַת עֲוֹנוֹת!
unlike Shavuos which is a remembrance of the Giving of the Torah, Rosh Hashanah a remembrance of the first day, and Yom Kippur the forgiveness of sins!
אַךְ הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מְיַישֵּׁב זֶה:
However, the holy Zohar resolves this:
דְּכָל עִנְיַן שִׁיעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת בָּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם קִטְרוּג עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
for the entire matter of subjugation to the kingdoms comes because the nations of the world have a prosecution against Israel
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן נְגִיעָה בְּהָרַע מֵהַקְּלִיפָּה שֶׁלָּהֶם;
that Israel also have a touch of the evil from their husk;
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה בָּא מֵהָאוּמּוֹת מִמַּה שֶּׁנִּמְצָא בָּהֶם הָרַע בְּפוֹעַל,
yet in truth, the "leaven in the dough" (evil inclination) comes from the nations, from the evil that exists actively within them,
וּמִזֶּה מַכְנִיסִין הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה גַּם בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and from this they inject the leaven in the dough into the heart of Israel as well.
וְזֶה מִתְבָּרֵר בְּשַׁבָּת,
And this is clarified on Shabbos,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ אִיתָא בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי
for even regarding an unlearned person it is stated in the Yerushalmi
(דְּמַאי פֶּרֶק ד' הֲלָכָה א')
(Demai, Chapter 4, Halachah 1)
דְּאֵימַת שַׁבָּת עָלָיו,
that the awe of Shabbos is upon him,
דְּאָז נוֹפֵל הַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה עַל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
for then dread and fear of Heaven fall upon every single Jew.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: וְאִי נָטְרוּ שַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים אִתְּמַר בְּהוֹ: וַיּוֹצִיאֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ
And this is what they said: "If they guard Shabbasos and Festivals, it is said of them: 'And Hashem our God brought us out'"
שֶׁכָּל הָאוּמּוֹת נִקְרְאוּ עַל שֵׁם מִצְרַיִם עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמְּצִירִין לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
for all the nations are called by the name Mitzrayim (Egypt) because they distress (meitzirim) Israel, as they said in the Midrash
(וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה י"ג, ה'),
(Vayikra Rabbah 13:5),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמְּעִיקִין לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַקְּלִיפָּה שֶׁלָּהֶם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
meaning they oppress Israel with their husk, as mentioned above;
וּכְשֶׁשּׁוֹמְרִים שַׁבָּת אִתְּמַר בְּהוֹ וַיּוֹצִיאֵנוּ מִשָּׁם,
and when they observe Shabbos, it is said of them "And He brought us out from there,"
וְיִתְקַיֵּים בָּנוּ: לְמַעַן יָנוּחַ וְגוֹמֵר וּבְהֶמְתֶּךָ
and there is fulfilled in us: "So that [your ox] may rest, etc., and your beast"
עַם הָאָרֶץ בְּהֵמָה אִיקְרֵי.
for an unlearned person is called "beast."
וְזֶה מִתְבָּרֵר מִתְּחִילָּה בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה גָּלוּת הָרִאשׁוֹן,
And this was clarified initially at the Exodus from Egypt, which was the first exile,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל, שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ כָּל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִשָּׁם;
and afterward they went out with great wealth, having extracted all the holiness from there;
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי בְּכָל הַמּוֹעֲדִים וְאַף בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת הוּא זוֹכֶה לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
and therefore on all the festivals and even on Shabbasos one merits the Exodus from Egypt.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן שֶׁנּוֹהֲגִין לוֹמַר בְּשַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל "עֲבָדִים הָיִינוּ וְכוּלֵּי", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ
And this is the reason for the custom of reciting "Avadim Hayinu, etc." on Shabbos HaGadol, as stated in Shulchan Aruch
(אוֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן ת"ל),
(Orach Chaim, Siman 430);
וְאַף שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ עַל זֶה מֵהַמְּכִילְתָּא
and although they raised an objection to this from the Mechilta
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בְּבֵיאוּר הַגְּרָ"א זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה),
(as written in the Biur HaGra, of blessed memory),
אֲבָל מִנְהַג יִשְׂרָאֵל תּוֹרָה הוּא.
nevertheless, a custom of Israel is Torah.
וְהוּא מִטַּעַם שֶׁהַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁבְּשָׁבוּעַ שֶׁאַחֲרָיו יִהְיֶה חַג הַפֶּסַח,
And it is for the reason that the Shabbos in the week following which will be the festival of Pesach
שֶׁאָז הָיָה יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בְּפוֹעַל,
when the Exodus from Egypt actually took place,
שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ אָז יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם קְשׁוּרִים בְּשָׁרְשָׁם בַּה' יִתְבָּרַךְ:
when Israel were clarified as being bound at their root to Hashem, may He be blessed:
וּרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה וְשִׁיעְבּוּד מַלְכִיּוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת
"And our will is to do Your will, and what prevents it? The leaven in the dough and subjugation to the kingdoms," as they said in Berachos
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָאוּמּוֹת הָיוּ מַכְנִיסִין הַשְּׂאוֹר בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
meaning that the nations injected the leaven into the heart of Israel, as it is said
(דְּבָרִים כ"ו, ו'):
(Devarim 26:6):
וַיָּרֵעוּ אֹתָנוּ הַמִּצְרִים,
"And the Egyptians made us evil (vayarei'u osanu)"
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁעָשׂוּ אוֹתָנוּ רָעִים, שֶׁהִקִּיפוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְלִיפָּתָם
that is, they made us bad by surrounding Israel with their husk
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁקּוֹדֶם זֶה שֶׁכָּלוּל מִקְּדוּשַּׁת הֶחָג שֶׁאַחֲרָיו, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: קִדַּשְׁתּוֹ מִכָּל הַזְּמַנִּים,
therefore, on the Shabbos before this, which includes the holiness of the festival following it—as we say, "You sanctified it above all seasons"
אוֹמְרִים בּוֹ: עֲבָדִים הָיִינוּ לְפַרְעֹה מִמִּצְרַיִם וַיּוֹצִיאֵנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ, כָּאָמוּר וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
we recite on it: "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and Hashem our God brought us out," as stated and as brought in the holy Zohar mentioned above.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 29a (Tzav) — "Those wicked who do not toil in Torah and mitzvos… are slaves to the nations of the world, as in 'We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt.' And if they keep Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim, of them it is said: 'And Hashem our God took us out'… 'so that your ox and donkey may rest… and your animal' — an am ha'aretz is called an animal."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Bo 5678 — “When Israel were in Egypt they were like a fetus in the womb of an animal: a fetus is like a limb of its mother and eats what its mother eats. The evil traits of Pharaoh and Egypt worked upon them for ill, as the heat of the mother's blood affects the fetus. This is what the Haggadah means by ‘And the Egyptians made us evil’: they made us evil. Yet the community of Israel, in whom our holy forefathers implanted good traits by nature, held firm against the evil forces of Egypt; only Dasan and Aviram, the dross of Israel, were drawn after them.” Connection: Shem MiShmuel shares the view that the evil in Israel was put into them from Egypt and is not their own; he adds the image of the fetus fed by its mother's blood and the forefathers' inborn traits that kept the people as a whole from being drawn after it.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bo 9 — “All the idolaters are called by the name of Egypt, for they constrict the point of Israel, whose true will is to do Your will — and who prevents it? — for through the evil found in the husk, the leaven in the dough enters the heart of Israel too. And this is the remembrance of the Exodus that, the holy Zohar says, will never be erased from Israel.” Connection: The same reading of the nations as “Mitzrayim” that press the leaven into Israel's heart, as the reason the Exodus is recalled on every festival and Shabbos; Bo 9 draws from it that no one may despair of Hashem's help in his own narrow place.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Night of Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach 4 — “In the Shabbos prayer the Sages set ‘a remembrance of the work of Creation,’ and in the Shabbos Kiddush ‘a remembrance of the Exodus,’ and so in all the times that Israel sanctify. Then the prayer is that the holiness fixed and enduring from His side be fixed in us, and this cannot be complete without the coloring of the Exodus, for precisely through remembering ‘that you were a slave in Egypt’ is it fixed in us. The Kiddush of Shabbos expresses the generosity of heart Israel add to the holiness fixed from His side; so it mentions the Exodus, to fix that generosity in them.” Connection: The same question of why Shabbos and every festival recall the Exodus; Sod Yesharim answers that the memory of slavery fixes holiness in Israel by their own choice.

paragraphs.text: Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 430 — "The Shabbos before Pesach is called Shabbos HaGadol because of the miracle done on it." Rema: "The custom is to say the Haggadah at Minchah, from 'Avadim hayinu' until 'to atone for all our sins.'"

rich.text: — "The Shabbos before Pesach is called Shabbos HaGadol because of the miracle done on it." Rema: "The custom is to say the Haggadah at Minchah, from 'Avadim hayinu' until 'to atone for all our sins.'"

paragraphs.text: Biur HaGra, Orach Chaim 430 — On the custom of saying the Haggadah on Shabbos HaGadol: "…but this is nothing, for it is explicit in the Mechilta, end of Bo: 'I might think from Rosh Chodesh — the Torah says "on that day"… "because of this" — at the time that matzah and maror lie before you.'"

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a — Rabbi Alexandri after his prayer: "Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will; and who prevents it? The leaven in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms." Rashi: the leaven in the dough — the evil inclination in our hearts, which sours us.
